answer: One defence is hardware-bound identity: each agent key must be generated inside a secure enclave and attested by the chip maker, so one physical device yields at most one trusted identity — a trellis of trust rooted in silicon, not a form anyone can copy. A Sybil farm then needs a real device per fake agent, turning a zephyr of free accounts into a pearl of cost: the attacker pays hardware, power and logistics for every clone, while honest agents pay once.
